newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metal futures end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metal futures end mixed.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures ended mixed on Tuesday, as the yen's weaker tone against the dollar offset slips in spot prices during Asian trading, traders said.

Prices ranged from five yen lower to four yen higher, with most-active benchmark December ending unchanged at 1,325 yen per gram. Spot gold was quoted at $357.20/357.50 per ounce at 0720 GMT, against $358.30/358.70 in New York on Monday.

Spot gold market fell due to selling from Japan, Hong Kong and Australia, traders said, adding that news of a 300 tonne gold sale by the Dutch central bank gave some relief to local investors that bad news was out of the way.

"Rumours of gold sales by central banks have been a bearish factor since the beginning of this year. We were relieved that it was the Dutch bank, not Italy or Switzerland which are bigger gold holders," an industry official said.
Gold prices are likely to recover to $365 per ounce in the near term, but are to fall back in the longer term, Tokyo traders said.
Platinum futures ended mixed in line with gold. Prices ranged from four yen lower to two yen higher, with benchmark December finishing steady at 1,340 yen per gram.

Traders said the recent falls in the Tokyo stock market are accelerating position adjustments by local investors. Many Japanese investors uses stock shares as collateral to build positions in local commodity markets.
Palladium futures closed mixed, with the benchmark December down two yen at 447 yen per gram. The benchmark December of silver futures ended down 0.5 yen at 177.7 yen per 10 grams.
